caption: What if you could snap your fingers and stop time for everyone except you? Physicists who play with this thought experiment find a lot of problems. Light would freeze too, so almost no new light would reach your eyes and the world would go dark. Sound is just moving air, so frozen air means total silence. Every cubic metre of air holds about 25 trillion trillion molecules, and if they were all stuck in place, the air around you would act like a solid wall: you couldn't walk or even breathe in. The plot twist: you can't stop time, but it really does tick at different speeds. Because of Einstein's relativity, clocks on GPS satellites run about 38 microseconds a day fast compared with clocks on the ground. Engineers correct for it, but without that fix your phone's map would drift by roughly 10 km every day. What would YOU do first with frozen time? 👇
